Subject: Checkout slowdowns — spikes in completion time since 07:30 PT

Hi Michael,

We're seeing a spike in completion times on Redwood API calls from our checkout flow starting ~07:30 PT this morning. P95s look fine but a subset of requests are taking 6–12s to finish which is causing checkout timeouts for ~0.6% of sessions. We've attached a small trace bundle and a sample request_ids list.

Steps we've taken: restarted our client workers (no effect), narrowed to a few request IDs (included). Can you confirm you're seeing this and advise next steps? This is impacting a small but revenue-critical set of customers.

Thanks,
Chris Nolan
SRE Lead, HelixCommerce

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Checkout slowdowns — spikes in completion time since 07:30 PT

Quick investigative note (initial):
- Observed the sample request_ids from Helix in our traces. Pattern: a cluster of requests hit a single Dedicated pool host and experienced heavy stall on the token-generation loop (p99 ~ 8.9s for affected shard).
- Telemetry: concurrency_cap reached 120 consistently on that host between 07:24–07:40 PT; autoscaler did not spin up additional capacity due to recent allocation limits on the Dedicated pool (customer cap).
- Runtime behavior: backlog induced repeated KV cache lookups and small scheduler thrashing — we see elevated system-level queue lengths and an increase in coroutine context switches.
- Error rates: 502s slightly up but mostly timeouts on client side. No model OOMs observed.

Immediate mitigations proposed (non-model changes):
1) Temporary bump Helix Dedicated concurrency_cap + burst quota for the next 90 minutes (evade cap-triggered backpressure).
2) Enable per-tenant prefix caching for repeated checkout prompts (low-risk toggle).
3) Route new checkout traffic to a sibling host in same region (manual reroute; fast).

Data artifacts attached to INF-5831: sample_traces.json, host_metrics_07_24_07_40.csv (uploaded).

I'll standby for approval to push the cap change and plan to monitor impact. If we see broader host saturation we'll trigger a canary rollback to the last stable runtime kernel selection.

Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Executive summary & actions — HelixCommerce elongated completions (INF-5831)

Folks — final update and exec note for this incident. Summary first:
- Incident window: 2027-06-21T07:24:00–2027-06-21T07:46:00 PT
- Impact: ~0.6% checkout sessions on Helix saw 6–12s completion windows; revenue impact isolated to specific storefronts (estimate under follow-up).
- Root cause (initial postmortem): localized host saturation in Helix Dedicated pool due to concurrency cap hits combined with a small request pattern that amplified KV cache churn and scheduler thrash. Not a model regression.

Actions taken:
1) Temporarily increased Helix Dedicated concurrency_cap by +40 for 90 minutes (safe, reversible). Observed p99 for affected shard drop from ~8.9s to ~1.2s within two minutes.
2) Routed new checkout traffic off the hot host and enabled prefix caching for the tenant; both reduced repeated compute on the hot path.
3) No customer-side change required; communicated with Helix (Marissa sent acknowledgement).

Requested exec decisions / follow-ups:
- Approve the proposed playbook in attached proposed-mitigation-playbook.md to automate cap-bumps and routing in future incidents (low-risk automation).
- Approve a one-week usage credit subject to verification (Marissa to finalize amount).
- Postmortem to be published to the incident channel by Friday; engineering to include telemetry thresholds that will auto-trigger scale actions (Dylan/Karthik).

Notes: We preserved SLA for the tier by avoiding model rollbacks; the fix was infra/serving config. This highlights the customer risk when Dedicated pool caps are conservative for bursty checkout traffic. We'll propose a recommended cap-sizing FAQ for Dedicated customers.

Attachments: proposed-mitigation-playbook.md, helix_trace_20270621.zip

—Michael Grant
Director, Customer Reliability
